DECISION: SPLIT into two children. Both are comparator-accepted DAG declarations with byte-identical frozen Lean types. The controller maps each key onto the existing accepted node, so no new node or worker is created. The selected theorem's own Lean proof reduces to supplied step 6, in three lines.

WHY. The supplied proof has two separable parts, and both are already proved in the DAG, on the slicing branch.
(i) Steps 2–5 never use a property of the standard basis:
- vanishing on non-injective tuples;
- sign invariance under permutations;
- the parametrization (σ, I) ↦ I∘σ of the injective tuples via Tuple.sort and StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT;
- the j!-fold reindexing.
For an arbitrary family u they are exactly the accepted counting identity slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_eq_factorial_mul (node root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1.count_sq_sum-a1, candidate 6c884a2c75285ef09b0d96d9ab4fee5fab26dbb2). Its accepted proof is the same argument, and its Lean proof is a single theorem of about 70 lines.
(ii) The conclusion of step 1, |γ|² = Σ_I (γ(e∘I)² if StrictMono I else 0), is the case u = EuclideanSpace.basisFun of the accepted slicing_mb_wn_norm_sq_eq_onb_sum (node root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1.onb_norm_sq-a1, candidate 66289299bceafab55148bb8a5f37d375b4b47e6e). Its accepted proof opens with the same Real.sq_sqrt argument.
Alternatives rejected:
- Keeping the node atomic would re-prove about 60 lines that duplicate an accepted proof. That alternative was also verified; see (d) below.
- A new thin node for step 1 would cost a fresh worker and decomposition session for a fact that is already accepted.

HOW THE CHILDREN GIVE THE SELECTED STATEMENT (supplied step 6). Fix m, j, γ and let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ.
- onb_norm_sq m j e γ: covectorEuclideanNorm γ ^ 2 = N, where N := Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m} (γ(e∘I)² if StrictMono I else 0).
- count_sq_sum m j ⇑e γ: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} γ(e∘i)² = j!·N.
- Substituting the first into the second gives Σ_i γ(e∘i)² = j!·|γ|².

  rw [Submission.slicing_mb_wn_norm_sq_eq_onb_sum m j (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ) γ]
  exact Submission.slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_eq_factorial_mul m j (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ) γ
Both children hold for all m and j, so the degenerate cases j = 0 and j > m need no separate treatment.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration. Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1.count_sq_sum-a1, declaration Submission.slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_eq_factorial_mul (status accepted, candidate commit 6c884a2c75285ef09b0d96d9ab4fee5fab26dbb2). It is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). It has no prerequisites, and within this split it depends on no sibling.

Role in the selected theorem iwl_sp_pn_sum_sq_tuples_eq_factorial_mul: this is exactly steps 2–5 of the supplied proof, for an arbitrary family u : Fin P → Eucl P in place of the standard basis:
- non-injective tuples contribute 0;
- F(i∘σ) = F(i);
- the parametrization (σ, β) ↦ β∘σ of the injective tuples;
- the reindexing that yields the factor j!.
Those steps use no property of the standard basis vectors e_c other than that they form a family of vectors. The parent applies this child with P := m, k := j, u := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ), φ := γ. The words "parent Step 1" in the title and "parent proof, Step 1" in the verbatim proof below refer to the accepted node's own parent, root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1, not to the selected theorem.

Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Source: parent proof, Step 1 (counting lemma), with the bijection and the sign computation written out.

Notation. [P] := {0,…,P−1}. u = (u_0,…,u_{P−1}) is an arbitrary family of vectors of ℝ^P; no orthonormality is used. φ is a k-covector, i.e. a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ. For I : {0,…,k−1} → [P] write u_I := (u_{I(0)},…,u_{I(k−1)}) and g(I) := φ(u_I)². Let Inc be the set of strictly increasing I and Inj the set of injective I. Let S_k be the group of permutations of {0,…,k−1}, so |S_k| = k!. The right-hand sum of the statement equals Σ_{β∈Inc} g(β), because its summand is g(I) for strictly increasing I and 0 otherwise. So the claim is Σ_{all I} g(I) = k!·Σ_{β∈Inc} g(β).

1. (Non-injective maps contribute 0.) Let I ∉ Inj and choose a ≠ b with I(a) = I(b). The tuple u_I then has the same vector in positions a and b, so j ↦ u_{I(j)} is not injective. Because φ is alternating, φ(u_I) = 0, so g(I) = 0. Hence Σ_{all I} g(I) = Σ_{I∈Inj} g(I).

2. (Permutation invariance.) For every I and σ ∈ S_k, u_{I∘σ} = u_I∘σ, the tuple u_I with its entries permuted by σ. Because φ is alternating, φ(u_I∘σ) = sign(σ)·φ(u_I) with sign(σ) ∈ {1, −1}. Therefore g(I∘σ) = sign(σ)²·φ(u_I)² = g(I).

3. (Parametrization of injective maps.) Define Φ : S_k × Inc → Inj by Φ(σ, β) := β∘σ.
 (a) Φ is well defined: β is strictly increasing, hence injective, and σ is bijective, so β∘σ is injective.
 (b) Φ is injective. Suppose β∘σ = β'∘σ'. Since σ and σ' are surjective, β and β' both have the image of β∘σ = β'∘σ' as their image. Two strictly increasing maps β, β' : {0,…,k−1} → [P] with the same image are equal. Indeed, if β ≠ β', let t be the least index with β(t) ≠ β'(t), say β(t) < β'(t). Then β(t) = β'(s) for some s. If s < t, then β'(s) = β(s) < β(t). If s ≥ t, then β'(s) ≥ β'(t) > β(t). Both are contradictions. So β = β'. Then β∘σ = β∘σ' and injectivity of β give σ = σ'.
 (c) Φ is surjective. Let I ∈ Inj. Its image s := I({0,…,k−1}) has exactly k elements. Let β be the increasing enumeration of s; it is a strictly increasing map {0,…,k−1} → [P] with image s, so β ∈ Inc. For each a, β(a) ∈ s, so β(a) = I(b) for a unique b =: τ(a). The map τ : {0,…,k−1} → {0,…,k−1} is injective because β is, so τ ∈ S_k, and I∘τ = β. Hence I = β∘τ⁻¹ = Φ(τ⁻¹, β).
 So Φ is a bijection.

4. (Summation.) Reindex along the bijection Φ (step 3), then use g(β∘σ) = g(β) (step 2):
 Σ_{I∈Inj} g(I) = Σ_{(σ,β)∈S_k×Inc} g(β∘σ) = Σ_{σ∈S_k} Σ_{β∈Inc} g(β) = k!·Σ_{β∈Inc} g(β).

5. (Conclusion.) Steps 1 and 4 give Σ_{all I} φ(u_I)² = k!·Σ_{β∈Inc} φ(u_β)² = k!·Σ_I (φ(u_I)² if I is strictly increasing, else 0). This is the claim. Degenerate cases are included. For k = 0, the only map is the empty map, which lies in both Inc and Inj, and |S_0| = 1 = 0!. For k > P, Inj = Inc = ∅ and both sides are 0. ∎

Formalization pointers (all present at the pinned Mathlib): ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective; AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to φ.toAlternatingMap; Tuple.sort, Tuple.monotone_sort, Monotone.strictMono_of_injective, Tuple.comp_perm_comp_sort_eq_comp_sort, Tuple.sort_eq_refl_iff_monotone (τ in step 3(c) can be taken as Tuple.sort I); Finset.sum_nbij' for the reindexing; Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin for |S_k| = k!.
proof_key_steps: Non-injective I give a tuple u_I with a repeated vector, so φ(u_I) = 0 because φ is alternating; the full sum reduces to injective I.
For a permutation σ, φ(u_{I∘σ}) = sign(σ)·φ(u_I), hence φ(u_{I∘σ})² = φ(u_I)².
(σ, β) ↦ β∘σ is a bijection from S_k × {strictly increasing β} onto the injective maps: equal images force β = β', and the increasing enumeration of the image gives surjectivity.
Σ_{I injective} φ(u_I)² = Σ_σ Σ_β φ(u_β)² = k!·Σ_{β strictly increasing} φ(u_β)².

In Lean the sum runs over all I : Fin k → Fin P, with summand 0 for I that are not strictly increasing. So SimonGMT's coefficient norm, defined with the standard basis, takes the same value in every orthonormal basis.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration. Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1.onb_norm_sq-a1, declaration Submission.slicing_mb_wn_norm_sq_eq_onb_sum (status accepted, candidate commit 66289299bceafab55148bb8a5f37d375b4b47e6e). It is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker).

Dependencies. Its accepted proof uses two results:
- count_sq_sum (Submission.slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_eq_factorial_mul). This is the sibling count_sq_sum of this split, hence depends_on = [count_sq_sum].
- parseval_sq_sum (Submission.slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_onb_invariant; DAG node root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1.parseval_sq_sum-a1, status accepted, candidate commit f12646af114b0f8ee6da768da27db2bdaa5773a9). This is not a sibling in this split. It is a retained accepted prerequisite: candidate 66289299 has both f12646af and 6c884a2 in its history (merged by b88d689 and 49a7c57 respectively). Its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim in the appendix below, so the argument is self-contained apart from the sibling count_sq_sum.

Role in the selected theorem: with P := m, k := j, u := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ, φ := γ, this child states covectorEuclideanNorm γ ^ 2 = Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m} (γ(e∘I)² if I is strictly increasing, else 0). That is exactly the conclusion of step 1 of the supplied proof, before the sum is rewritten over the subtype S. Step 1 of the verbatim proof below is the same argument as the first part of the supplied step 1 (Real.sq_sqrt applied to the nonnegative defining sum). Several words in the title and verbatim proof refer to the accepted node's own parent root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1 and its children, not to this split:
- "parent Step 3" in the title;
- "parent proof" and "sibling results" in the verbatim proof.
There, "count_sq_sum" and "parseval_sq_sum" denote the accepted declarations named above.

Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Source: parent proof, Step 3. It uses the sibling results count_sq_sum (parent Step 1, Lean slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_eq_factorial_mul) and parseval_sq_sum (parent Step 2, Lean slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_onb_invariant).

Notation. e = (e_0,…,e_{P−1}) is the standard basis of ℝ^P (e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i); it is an orthonormal basis. For a family w = (w_0,…,w_{P−1}) and a k-covector φ, put φ(w_I) := φ(w_{I(0)},…,w_{I(k−1)}), N_w(φ) := Σ_{all I : {0,…,k−1}→[P]} φ(w_I)² and Σ^<_w(φ) := Σ_I (φ(w_I)² if I is strictly increasing, else 0). Let u be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P. Claim: covectorEuclideanNorm(φ)² = Σ^<_u(φ).

1. By definition, covectorEuclideanNorm(φ) = √(Σ^<_e(φ)). Every summand of Σ^<_e(φ) is a square or 0, so Σ^<_e(φ) ≥ 0. Therefore covectorEuclideanNorm(φ)² = Σ^<_e(φ).

2. Apply count_sq_sum to the family u (the basis vectors u_0,…,u_{P−1}) and to the family e: N_u(φ) = k!·Σ^<_u(φ) and N_e(φ) = k!·Σ^<_e(φ).

3. Apply parseval_sq_sum to the orthonormal bases u and e: N_u(φ) = N_e(φ).

4. Steps 2 and 3 give k!·Σ^<_u(φ) = k!·Σ^<_e(φ). Since k! ≥ 1, k! ≠ 0 and it cancels: Σ^<_u(φ) = Σ^<_e(φ). By step 1 this equals covectorEuclideanNorm(φ)². ∎

Formalization pointers: unfold covectorEuclideanNorm and use Real.sq_sqrt with Finset.sum_nonneg. The definition's summand is literally (φ (fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i))) ^ 2 under the same StrictMono decidability instance. So the sibling statements instantiated with the family ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ), and with v := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ, match it syntactically. Cancel with Nat.factorial_ne_zero and mul_left_cancel₀.

--- Appendix: verbatim accepted proof of the retained prerequisite parseval_sq_sum (Submission.slicing_mb_wn_sq_sum_onb_invariant: for all P, k ∈ ℕ, any two orthonormal bases u, v of ℝ^P and every k-covector φ on ℝ^P, Σ_{all I : Fin k → Fin P} φ(u_I)² = Σ_{all I : Fin k → Fin P} φ(v_I)². In it, "parent" again refers to root.slicing-a1.slice_mass_bound-a1.wedge_norm-a1, which used v = e.) ---

Source: parent proof, Step 2 (basis independence of N). It is stated here for two arbitrary orthonormal bases u and v. The parent uses v = e, the standard basis; the argument is the same.

Notation. [P] := {0,…,P−1}; ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm of ℝ^P. u = (u_0,…,u_{P−1}) and v = (v_0,…,v_{P−1}) are orthonormal bases of ℝ^P. φ is a k-covector, a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ; only multilinearity is used. For a family w and I : {0,…,k−1} → [P] put φ(w_I) := φ(w_{I(0)},…,w_{I(k−1)}) and N_w(φ) := Σ_{all I} φ(w_I)². Claim: N_u(φ) = N_v(φ).

1. (Parseval in one slot.) For every linear functional ℓ : ℝ^P → ℝ, Σ_{i∈[P]} ℓ(u_i)² = Σ_{i∈[P]} ℓ(v_i)². Proof: by the Riesz representation on ℝ^P, ℓ = ⟨a, ·⟩ for some a ∈ ℝ^P. For any orthonormal basis w of ℝ^P, a = Σ_i ⟨a, w_i⟩ w_i, so |a|² = Σ_i ⟨a, w_i⟩² (Parseval). Hence Σ_i ℓ(u_i)² = Σ_i ⟨a, u_i⟩² = |a|² = Σ_i ⟨a, v_i⟩² = Σ_i ℓ(v_i)². Both sums equal the squared operator norm ‖ℓ‖² = |a|²; every linear functional on ℝ^P is continuous.

2. (Hybrid sums.) For r = 0, 1, …, k and I : {0,…,k−1} → [P], let w^{r,I} be the k-tuple with entries w^{r,I}_j := v_{I(j)} for j < r and w^{r,I}_j := u_{I(j)} for j ≥ r. Put M_r := Σ_{all I} φ(w^{r,I})². Since w^{0,I} = u_I and w^{k,I} = v_I, M_0 = N_u(φ) and M_k = N_v(φ).

3. (One slot at a time: M_r = M_{r+1} for r < k.) Fix r < k. The maps I : {0,…,k−1} → [P] correspond bijectively to pairs (i, I'), where i := I(r) ∈ [P] and I' is the restriction of I to {0,…,k−1}∖{r}. For fixed I', set x_j := v_{I'(j)} for j < r and x_j := u_{I'(j)} for j > r. Define ℓ_{I'}(z) := φ(x_0,…,x_{r−1}, z, x_{r+1},…,x_{k−1}); this is a linear functional on ℝ^P because φ is linear in its r-th argument. If I corresponds to (i, I'), then w^{r,I} and w^{r+1,I} both have entry x_j in every position j ≠ r: for j < r both use v_{I(j)}, and for j > r both use u_{I(j)}. Their r-th entries are u_i and v_i respectively. Hence φ(w^{r,I}) = ℓ_{I'}(u_i) and φ(w^{r+1,I}) = ℓ_{I'}(v_i). Summing first over i ∈ [P] and then over I', and applying step 1 to each ℓ_{I'}:
 M_r = Σ_{I'} Σ_{i∈[P]} ℓ_{I'}(u_i)² = Σ_{I'} Σ_{i∈[P]} ℓ_{I'}(v_i)² = M_{r+1}.

4. (Conclusion.) By step 3, N_u(φ) = M_0 = M_1 = ⋯ = M_k = N_v(φ). For k = 0 the chain is trivial: both sides equal φ()², the value on the empty tuple. For P = 0 and k ≥ 1 both sums are empty. ∎

Remark (the same slot-by-slot replacement, organized for Lean). Run it as an induction on k, for all k-covectors at once. In degree k+1, write φ(z_0, z_1,…,z_k) = ψ_{z_0}(z_1,…,z_k), where ψ_z := φ(z, ·,…,·) is a k-covector (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft, curryLeft_apply_apply). Split I into (I(0), J) with J := (I(1),…,I(k)) (Fin.consEquiv, Fintype.sum_prod_type). Replace u by v in the last k slots by applying the induction hypothesis to each ψ_{u_i}. Exchange the two sums (Finset.sum_comm). Finally, replace u_i by v_i in slot 0 by step 1 applied to ℓ_J(z) := ψ_z(v_J), the continuous linear functional (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ ℝ^P ℝ v_J) ∘ curryLeft φ. Step 1 is Mathlib's OrthonormalBasis.norm_dual: ‖ℓ‖² = Σ_i ℓ(w_i)² for every orthonormal basis w.
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm(φ)² = Σ^<_e(φ), because the radicand is a sum of nonnegative terms.
count_sq_sum: N_u(φ) = k!·Σ^<_u(φ) and N_e(φ) = k!·Σ^<_e(φ).
